body:
I'm not sure this will work, the object is already freed so calling anything on it will segfault, the issue lies higher up in the call I think

This also feels very specific, unless this function somehow is the only one that is affected by this 

This will only work as long as the memory location hasn't been overwritten yet, it relies on that the memory is still valid even if the object is freed, it won't work otherwise

> This will only work as long as the memory location hasn't been overwritten yet, it relies on that the memory is still valid even if the object is freed, it won't work otherwise

Hm, yeah that does seem like a good point; I tested it against the MRP case provided in the issue and it worked reliably there, but it hadn't occurred to me that there could be scenarios with much longer spans of time between freeing the object and passing it into `tween_property()`. 

At first I was confused by your saying

> the issue lies higher up in the call I think

as this seemed about as high up in the call stack as it could be (`tween_property()` is being called directly from the GDScript code). But thinking more about it, I think it's making more sense to me that GDScript uses its own call stack system, and perhaps somewhere in there, it could validate that an `Object` being passed through is valid/not queued for deletion...? I'm still not sure exactly how that would work at this point, but perhaps it is a start 😅

This *should* be caught by the internal VM system for arguments, not sure, though not sure this is actually a bug as it's clearly invalid usage and shouldn't be done this way. The more I think about it the less I think this is a bug and more of an enhancement with potentially expensive overhead to handle invalid usage, and that's probably why nothing catches this already

The general solution would probably be to use `get_validated_object` when processing the arguments for methods, not sure exactly what it does internally, it might just use the raw pointer for performance, if that is the case that's by design I'd say

It *could* be something with the `RequiredParam` system, haven't looked closely there, would be relevant to test older versions from when this took an `Object` instead of `RequiredParam`

It *might* be because of this:
https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/51105ccbe58381774ecd7a7486d564b202a5192e/core/object/object.h#L1149-L1156

This means we don't do memory safe conversions here when casting, not sure if that was done intentionally or not though, try changing it to use the same cast as the ones above it (the `RefCounted` derived ones), that should probably make things fail cleanly without these changes
